scope: Connected contact-first dual-arm carrier, MiniMax-H3 test-time scaling, and bounded material-protection audit for ordered T-shirt folding
summary: A synthetic fixed-base planar dual-arm carrier was compiled from the supplied first frame with complete per-frame node chains, q/qdot, conserved link lengths, bounded joint and tip steps, and named gripper contact before each sleeve moved. The frozen MiniMax-H3 policy then generated two 32-step candidates and one 40-step repair candidate. All three passed contact causality, exact first frame, continuity, bundle transport, background, and terminal compactness, but all three failed both sleeve-length gates, viewer-left-before-viewer-right tracking, and body-after-sleeves tracking. Native-resolution contact sheets show H3 stretching the black sleeves into long strips, so no H3 candidate is accepted. A bounded hybrid that restored the analytic shirt support after H3 also failed the independent visual gates and is retained only as a rejected experiment. The articulated carrier is useful proposal-control evidence but is not promoted as a final photorealistic video.
evidence: Analytic carrier metrics: maximum link-length error 6.394884621840902e-14 pixels, maximum joint step 0.1732065255923385 radians, maximum tip step 16.56505804922376 pixels
All three H3 candidates report contact_precedes_cloth_motion=true and both sleeve-length gates=false
Candidate 1 was the diagnostic best but its maximum sleeve-length relative deviations were 1.4479370908954579 viewer-left and 0.4952819656115264 viewer-right against the unchanged 0.08 threshold
lessons: Adding connected articulated manipulator motion and contact timing repaired the previous carrier's self-moving-cloth failure: every H3 candidate passed the frozen 2-D contact-causality gate.

Increasing the repair candidate from 32 to 40 steps did not improve either sleeve invariant and slightly worsened both maximum relative deviations, so more seeds or steps are not a justified next action.

A 2-D analytic carrier can make link and declared material-path conservation exact while still being visually inadequate for photorealistic H3 transfer; analytic proposal gates cannot replace independent output gates.

Post-H3 material restoration is not automatically safe: repeated encoding, moving-mask seams, tracker loss, and poor source carrier appearance can regress first-frame and background gates even when analytic transforms are exact.
limitations: The two planar rigs are synthetic camera-frame mechanisms because no exact pictured-robot URDF/MJCF or calibrated camera was available; their q/qdot are not real-robot joint commands.
The contact gate is 2-D visual proximity and temporal causality, not force, grasp stability, collision safety, or sensor-confirmed contact.
The protected hybrid preserves declared carrier pixels but failed the frozen visual evaluator and native-resolution plausibility review; it is not an accepted deliverable.
No MiniMax-H3 output in this experiment passes every immutable material and task-order gate.
next_actions: Replace raster articulation with a calibrated 3-D robot-and-cloth control render or a model with explicit dense correspondence/material-coordinate conditioning before spending more H3 seeds.
Design an occlusion-aware material tracker prospectively on held-out synthetic rotations, freeze it before generation, and keep the 0.08 sleeve threshold unchanged.
Use H3 only for bounded appearance refinement after the structured renderer is visually acceptable; preserve the original first frame without a second lossy encode.
